Long-running architectural facts, not incidents: ILO /availableconstraint/ returns 500 (constraints come via ?references=all); ECB does not support /availableconstraint/ (404 is expected, not an error); ESTAT has no practical constraint support; ESTAT direct json check is skipped by design (Eurostat returns 406 for SDMx-JSON); IMF direct json check is skipped by design (IMF ignores the JSON Accept header and returns XML); STATSNZ direct json check is skipped by design (Stats NZ ignores the JSON Accept header and returns CSV); BIS/ILO/IMF references:contentconstraint reads ignored (accepted and silently dropped); encoding:structure_xml Content-Type charset/version parameter order flips cosmetically from time to time across ABS/FBOS/ILO/SBS/OECD, verdict stays ok as always.
